name: Collaboration

subjectOf.text: Co-creation partnerships between developers and non-developers will be crucial to building a better digital future, and understanding coding is what enables lawyers to engage constructively with coders, programmers and other software developers.
subjectOf.abstract: "Co-creation" involving partnerships between developers and non- developers will be crucial to building a "better" digital future. And understanding coding enables lawyers to constructively engage with coders, programmers, and other software developers.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in a Digital Age Why 'Coding for Lawyers' Matters (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227967

subjectOf.text: Smart contracts undermine the ability of counterparties to continue collaborating when unanticipated eventualities arise, because in most cases of unfulfilled parameters the smart contract will simply cancel out.

subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Commerce – A Primer on Why Decentralized Reputation Verification Systems Are Needed (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3405401

subjectOf.text: Dynamic power organization in a DAO succeeds only if the decentralized governance structure motivates token holders to collaborate productively by fairly rewarding development, work, and the policing of any diminishments.
subjectOf.abstract: The successful implementation of such dynamic power organization requires a decentralized governance structure that motivates DAO token holders to collaborate productively, by fairly rewarding development, work, and the policing of any diminishments.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Blockchain-Based Corporate Governance (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3441904
scope_conditions: DAO designs that distribute autonomous power to members

subjectOf.text: Independent and autonomous subgroups, formed randomly based on members' ability to contribute to a common cause and characterized by equality and mutual trust, form the backbone of decentralized structures.
subjectOf.abstract: Independent and autonomous subgroups create the backbone of decentralized structures. Subgroups are formed randomly based on individual members' ability to contribute to the common cause of the group.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Preface to (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782191

subjectOf.text: When currency is the entire proximal goal of a transaction, all participants naturally behave as selfishly as possible and exploit any opportunity for individual profit at the group's expense, which makes cash profit a bad immediate incentive for both business and government.
subjectOf.abstract: If the entire proximal goal of a transaction is currency, all participants will naturally be- have in the most selfish manner possible, exploiting any opportunity for individual profit at the expense of the group.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Governance (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782214
scope_conditions: anonymous members staking currency on rigid smart contracts

subjectOf.text: The absence of a dedicated discussion platform, combined with poor engagement on third party accounts, hinders meaningful discussion and collaboration within a DAO, as scored for BrainDAO with an organizational communication score of 1 despite high decentralization and attack resistance scores.
subjectOf.abstract: The absence of a dedicated discussion platform and poor engagement on third-party accounts hinder meaningful discussions and collaboration (O: 1).
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Market Meta Analysis 2024 (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5254152
scope_conditions: DAOs communicating only through external social platforms

subjectOf.text: Solving data bias, computational overhead, stale datasets, privacy constraints, and inequitable compensation cannot be done within any single discipline; it requires concerted interdisciplinary effort across governments, corporations, researchers, and civil society.
subjectOf.abstract: addressing the challenges outlined herein—data bias, high computational overhead, stagnant or outdated datasets, privacy and security constraints, and inequitable compensation structures—requires concerted, interdisciplinary efforts.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Artificial Intelligence The Final Frontier (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5095633
